title: Probing quasiperiodic spectral accessibility with a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle
authors: Shujie Cheng, Lucas C. Céleri, Norton G. de Almeida, Gao Xianlong, G. D. de Moraes Neto
abstract: Quasiperiodic systems combine sharply different spectral and localisation regimes with a dense hierarchy of dynamical time scales. We show that a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle can use this structure as a thermodynamic probe, revealing which parts of the spectrum become dynamically accessible and thermodynamically relevant during a driven transformation. For a generalised Aubry-André-Harper chain, the resulting response is not determined by the static quasiperiodic regime alone: extended, near-critical, and crossing protocols do not exhibit universal ordering of work fluctuations. Instead, the statistics reflect transition pathways that are simultaneously dynamically coupled, thermally occupied, and energetically significant. The same spectral accessibility separates thermodynamic recovery from microscopic adiabatic recovery. Positive mean work can reappear while the population transfer dynamics remain strongly nonadiabatic because finite-rate population transfer is redistributed toward energetically less costly channels rather than suppressed. The full work distribution reveals a further separation, with a finite rate window in which positive-work cycles form a majority although the mean work remains negative. This behaviour persists in finite-size analysis. A thermally weighted spectral susceptibility connects these effects to a distributed hierarchy of dynamically active spectral regions rather than to a single minimum-gap bottleneck. Finite thermal contacts preserve this picture while introducing a second time scale and intercycle memory. Quantum Otto cycles can therefore provide a fluctuation-resolved thermodynamic probe of quasiperiodic spectral accessibility, complementary to direct spectroscopic and eigenstate-resolved diagnostics.
summary: This paper introduces the use of a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle as a novel thermodynamic probe for quasiperiodic systems. By analyzing work fluctuations, the authors show that the system's energy accessibility during driving depends on dynamic pathways rather than static spectral features. This offers a fluctuation-resolved method complementary to standard spectroscopic techniques.
main_problem: To use a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle as a thermodynamic probe to investigate which parts of the spectrum in quasiperiodic systems become dynamically accessible and thermodynamically relevant during a driven transformation.
main_result: The work statistics are determined by the dynamic transition pathways across the spectrum, not just the static quasiperiodic regime, revealing a distributed hierarchy of active spectral regions.
method: The authors analyze the quantum Otto cycle by treating the driving rate as a control parameter, examining work fluctuations, and comparing finite-rate dynamics to static limits.
model_or_system: The study uses the generalized Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) chain, a model for quasiperiodic lattices, subjected to a quantum Otto cycle protocol involving hot and cold baths.
key_observables: Mean work, work fluctuations (full distribution), thermally weighted spectral susceptibility, and population map distances (Dad, Dsud).
important_parameters: Finite driving rate, reservoir temperatures ($T_c, T_h$), and the quasiperiodic modulation strength ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on single-particle dynamics and assumes the applicability of the Otto cycle framework to probe spectral accessibility.
figures_summary: The notes mention comparisons of work statistics across different protocols (e.g., crossing vs. static) and the development of diagnostic tools like population map distances.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by defining the finite-rate cycle, analyzing the work statistics and fluctuations, and then applying this diagnostic tool to the quasiperiodic AAH chain to map spectral accessibility.
why_interesting: The connection between non-equilibrium thermodynamics (Otto cycles) and spectral properties (quasiperiodicity) provides a powerful, measurable diagnostic tool for understanding energy flow in complex quantum systems.
